findings.description: PolicyGuard rejection on missing data uses 'SHOULD' instead of 'MUST'. For a fail-closed safety gate, permissive normative language allows non-compliant implementations that do not reject on missing data.

evidence.quote: PolicyGuard SHOULD reject when data is missing.

findings.proposed_fix: Replace 'SHOULD' with 'MUST': 'PolicyGuard MUST reject when data is missing.'

findings.description: AT-999 is referenced inline but no acceptance test with that identifier is defined or linked in this fixture or a canonical AT registry. A broken AT cross-reference removes verifiable proof that the clause is tested.
findings.proposed_fix: Either define AT-999 in the canonical acceptance-test registry and link it, or remove the reference and replace with a valid AT-ID.

findings.description: The clause specifies rejection when data is missing but does not specify which safe trading mode (ReduceOnly or Kill) PolicyGuard must enter. Without an explicit safe-mode outcome the fail-closed behavior is underspecified and implementations may diverge.

evidence.quote: PolicyGuard SHOULD reject when data is missing.

findings.proposed_fix: Add: 'When data is missing PolicyGuard MUST set TradingMode to ReduceOnly and hold until the missing input is restored.'
